div.p: The undersigned, minister ad interim of exterior relations, has the honor to respond to the indication contained in the communication of your excellency of date the 21st instant in the following terms:

The national government has applied the 13 per cent, of the forty unities of the custom-house revenue to the payment of the reclamations called diplomatic, and in making the distribution it has foreseen the case that the said revenue for supervening causes might not come up to the sum estimated. Thus it has reserved monthly a sum (cantidad) which might serve, in necessary case, to equalize the estimates. And this was the base of the first distribution, and also of the last, which the government of the republic cannot less than maintain before the foreign governments.

To pay in this respect 95,000 bolivars monthly, instead of the 80,000 which are being paid, would be to exceed the estimate, for which the government is not authorized; and to offer to pay the excess, if there should be such, would be to promise its application to an object distinct from public instruction and improvements (el fomento) to which it is destined.

This destination given to the overplus revenue is the result of the wisest foresight, since precisely that which guarantees peace in the republic, and with it the fulfillment of the compromises contracted is principally among us the investment of the largest sum possible in public works, which on the other hand contribute much to the augmentation of the revenue.

For the rest, if it has offered to the Government of the United States to pay, through its intermediation, to the creditor governments (pagar por su intermedio á los Gobiernos acreedores), the total product of the 13 per cent, expressed in the estimate (presupuesto), that is to say, the sum of 1,040,000 bolivars instead of 960,000, thus giving away the sum (cantidad) which is now reserved, it has been with the object of facilitating the acceptance, even in exchange for exposing itself to having a deficit in the estimate (presupuesto). This proposition the Government of Venezuela will be prompt to maintain, and it cherishes the hope that the Government of Washington will find it reasonable, so much the more if your excellency deigns to recommend its acceptance, transmitting it with the appreciations which your enlightened judgment (criterio) may suggest.
